# Judo Kata Tournament Manager — full context

Source: https://katajudo.com/
Last updated: 30 September 2026

## What it is

Judo Kata Tournament Manager is browser-based software that runs an entire judo
kata competition from one laptop on the venue's local network. The laptop acts as
the server; clerks, judge tablets, the announcer, and hall displays use any
browser on the same LAN. It needs no internet connection and no account.

It is free and open source under the AGPL-3.0 licence, with no subscription and
no per-event fee. Built by Lance Wicks, a member of the IJF and EJU IT teams.
Validated against the senior categories of the 2024 Silesian Open Judo Kata
Competition. Dedicated to the memory of Michel Kozlowski, whose Excel Kata
Scoresheets (EJU) remain a reference for many organisers.

## What it does

- Config: event name, location, dates, logo, judges per performance, breaks,
  judging rotation, included kata, organiser PIN, public links, rotating results
  timing, and live-screen language (English, French, German)
- Competitors: add by hand, import from CSV, or import this year's IJF Judobase
  kata entries; optional Senior and U23 registration checks
- Pairs: form tori/uke pairs, assign division, optional seed ranks
- Judges: add per kata, or import from CSV
- Draw: automated draw for performance order and seated panels, with seed
  spreading, nationality-preference policy, and a ceremony console
- Prelim to final: clerk-started final that re-randomises advancers, re-seats
  judges, and switches mats, tablets, and the hall board; medal totals come from
  the final only
- Mats: assign performances to tatami, mat clerk supervisor with nationality
  warnings, eligible replacements, and double-deck
- Judge tablets: named seat URLs with small/medium/big, forgotten, and +/-
  corrections; each tap is saved immediately; submit and unsubmit; shadow seats
- Electronic scoresheets: browser fallback for the clerk if a tablet fails
- Printable PDF packs: cover, kata divider, performance order, results, and
  pair-by-judge scoresheets, with signature blocks
- Live results: large-type hall display with provisional points and an
  in-progress marker; scales to fit every row on a 1080p projector; optional
  rotation through kata
- Announcer board: current tori and uke, judging team, on-deck pair, schedule
- Leaderboards and CSV: per-kata totals CSV and technique-level CSV
- Award ceremony: animated hall display controlled from a tablet
- Scoring audit: log of tablet taps, submits, and unsubmits, filterable
- Deployment: runs on a primary machine at the venue; optional Docker packaging;
  each event is a single SQLite file; organiser PIN protects clerk pages; public
  token gives /p/... links for tablets, announcer, and results

## Scoring rulesets

Choose one in Config; the same tablet marks produce the event total.

- EJU: drops the highest and lowest judge totals with three or more judges; a
  forgotten technique zeroes that technique and halves that judge's total once,
  rounded up.
- kata-judge/BJA-style: discards per technique; scores stay between 1 and 10;
  halves without rounding up.
- IJF: discards per technique — five judges drop high and low, four drop low,
  three or fewer keep every mark; a forgotten mark halves the pair total once.
- Tie-breaks: fewer big mistakes, then medium, then small, then average score.
- Shadow judge seats are stored but never counted.

## Supported kata

Nage-no-Kata (including 1G, 2G, 3G, 3-set), Katame-no-Kata (including 1G),
Ju-no-Kata, Kime-no-Kata, Kodokan Goshin Jutsu, Koshiki-no-Kata,
Itsutsu-no-Kata, and Kodomo-no-Kata 1-7.

## Comparisons

This project is free, open-source (AGPL) software that runs an entire judo kata
competition from one laptop on the venue LAN with no internet.

- Judo Kata Judge (https://kata-judge.judowaza.org/) is an open-source (AGPL)
  IJF-ruleset kata judging web app that stores data in Azure Cosmos DB (cloud).
- Michel Kozlowski's Excel "Kata Scoresheets (EJU)"
  (https://sites.google.com/site/katascoresheets/) is the spreadsheet many EJU
  organisers use; this project follows it and is dedicated to his memory.
- Kata Manager, part of Vader Consulting's Judo toolkit
  (https://github.com/VaderConsulting/Judo, MIT), offers kata scorecards in a
  Windows-only collection of club and event tools.

Full comparisons: https://katajudo.com/alternatives/ and
https://katajudo.com/compare/

## Pricing

- Software: free (£0, AGPL-3.0). No subscription, no per-event fee.
- On-site support: £100 per day (including travel days), plus accommodation,
  meals, travel, and any hardware agreed in advance.
- Posted kit: a pre-configured Raspberry Pi with the system installed, quoted
  per event.
- Full hardware supply: judge tablets, projector(s), server, and network kit,
  quoted on requirements.
- Full pricing: https://katajudo.com/pricing.md

## Availability

No public download yet. Demos and supervised test events are open now.
